subject: Business Models
title: What Makes a Marketplace
description: A short lesson to help you apply What Makes a Marketplace.

hook.text: A marketplace doesn't sell products. It sells the connection between buyers and sellers.

buildup.text: Amazon Marketplace, Airbnb, and Uber all follow the same structure: match supply with demand, take a cut.

discovery.text: The marketplace's core value is reducing search costs. Before eBay, finding rare items meant driving to flea markets.

twist.text: Marketplaces can become more powerful than the sellers on them. Amazon's rules override individual brands.

climax.text: Owning the marketplace is more valuable than owning inventory. Power flows to the matchmaker.

punchline.text: Don't sell the product. Sell the connection. Marketplaces own the middle.

quiz.question: What is the core value a marketplace provides?
options: Reducing search costs between buyers and sellers
